text: In 1972, the Strongsville City School District in Strongsville, Ohio, rejected Joseph Heller's Catch-22 for use as a textbook and ordered it removed from the school library; according to the school, the reason was profane and inappropriate language. On appeal, a court upheld the school board’s right to reject Catch-22 from the curriculum but found its removal from the library unconstitutional. The novel was challenged in Dallas, TX, in 1974, and in Snoqualmie, WA, in 1979 because of its many references to women as “whores.”
meta_description: Catch-22 by Joseph Heller: removed from a Strongsville, Ohio school library in 1972; a court found the removal unconstitutional. Challenged in 1974, 1979.
